result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_weakly_connected_components()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count weakly connected components in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21568-L21604){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For undirected graphs, counts regular connected components. For directed graphs, treats all edges as undirected (ignoring direction) when finding components. A weakly connected component is a maximal set of nodes where every node is reachable from every other node when edge directions are ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of weakly connected components. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two separate pairs of nodes, with no edges between them, form two components: ::: {#5ca5b82e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("X", "Y") ) # Returns 2 graph.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
